about: P45A T11 judge calibration over the dev panel, 8 Oct 2026. Side A = main 0714a352 (own worktree, next start on 3218), side B = HEAD of P45A (3217); P45A does not touch game code, so both sides play the same games. Pacing clips with --gpu, judge = codex exec (subscription) through judge-sheet ask in an empty dir with sheet.png + schema only. One question version, one run each; no retry was needed.

nullTest.finding: 38/40 ties: the game code and the robot are deterministic, so A and B produce the same clips and the judge calls them a tie. The null test therefore shows the judge does not invent a difference between identical games; leftWinShare rests on 2 decided pairs and says nothing about position bias – read that from the sensitivity test.

sensitivity.command: run --set p45-panel --only d04,f01,f02,f03,f05,f10,h02,m01,m02,m11,n02,u06 --run p45a-idle --pace-clip --idle --draft-only --gpu; pairwise --a p45a-idle --b p45a-null-b --only <same>
sensitivity.a: the same game with the robot not started (--idle)
sensitivity.b: the game played by the robot (p45a-null-b)

pairs.why: Game A builds from distant targets to several nearby red enemies, with visible effects around the player before it ends. Game B stays mostly empty throughout, with the player aiming left and right and only an occasional visible shot, so it shows less danger and buildup.

Game B shows the player moving across the arena amid large yellow projectiles and orange enemies, with nearby threats and varied action continuing into the final rows. Game A keeps the player near the center with mostly distant glowing rings and sparse white shots, making its pace and buildup look more repetitive.

Game A keeps showing action, with the nearby obstacle alternating between upright and airborne positions and the robot extending its blue weapon near the end. Game B shows a bright flash around the robot at 7.5 seconds but ends before the next frame, giving it less visible variety or buildup.

Game B builds from distant targets to several enemies closer to the player, with bright impact effects before it ends, suggesting more action and danger. Game A stays largely unchanged for much longer, with sparse distant threats and only occasional shots.

Game A shows sustained movement, glowing projectiles, and multiple rock-like enemies closing in later, giving it more action and a stronger buildup. Game B shows a brief close encounter but ends soon afterward, with less visible variety or escalation.

Game B shows several enemies crowding and chasing the player, with bright attack effects and action continuing into the final rows. Game A mostly shows one enemy directly ahead of the player with little change before ending, making its pace and danger feel flatter.

Game A keeps moving through changing groups of furniture, carts, and orange animals, with animals drawing close around the player and obstacles continuing into the later scenes. Game B has a large shelf looming close by 7.5 seconds, but ends before the next frame, giving it much less sustained action or buildup.

Game A’s two orange threats close around the white player by 13.5 seconds, then the game ends. Game B shows movement across more of the arena and builds from two threats to three later on, offering a longer, more varied chase with continuing danger.

Game A shows the player moving around the arena, with orange enemies sometimes nearby and yellow projectiles scattered across changing positions. Game B has a busy opening, but afterward the player stays near the center with mostly distant glowing rings and little visible escalation.

Game A shows more movement, with the character reaching the far wall before the game ends. Game B lasts longer but stays mostly on the same character in an empty field, with no visible nearby threats or escalating action.

Game B keeps the player moving around the arena as orange enemies regroup and increase to three, sustaining pursuit and building pressure late in play. Game A has a close encounter with two enemies near the center, but ends shortly afterward with much less action overall.

Game B shows the red car moving around crates and scattered green threats throughout the sequence, with nearby encounters continuing into the final frames. Game A begins obscured by fog, shows a brief close encounter near the center, and ends before 19.5 seconds, offering less sustained action.
